claims: "Apollo 2" was not an officially designated mission.
"Apollo 2" is the informal name for the uncrewed AS-202 suborbital flight.
The AS-202 suborbital flight was launched on August 25, 1966.
AS-202 was part of the Saturn IB test program.
AS-202 successfully tested the Apollo command module’s heat shield.
AS-202 successfully tested the Apollo command module’s systems before human flight.
No mission was officially designated Apollo 2.
AS-202's mission goal was suborbital test of the Block I command/service module.
AS-202 focused on heat shield endurance, guidance, and fuel cells.
AS-202 used a Saturn IB launch vehicle.
The AS-202 spacecraft was recovered in the Pacific Ocean.
AS-202 reached an altitude of roughly 660 nautical miles.
After the 1967 Apollo 1 tragedy, NASA reordered the program's schedule.
NASA decided to start with Apollo 4 for the first Saturn V flight.
The officially recognized Apollo sequence jumped from Apollo 1 to 4.
AS-202 and AS-203 were never officially re-christened as "Apollo 2" or "Apollo 3" in the final record.
